plan.title: Treatment x time interaction in 12-sample cell-line RNA-seq
plan.analytical_narrative: The question — does the treatment effect differ between the two time points — is a two-factor interaction question on a 2 (condition) x 2 (time: t0, t1) design with 3 replicates per cell, 12 samples total, 12000 genes, raw Salmon gene-level counts in counts.csv keyed by gene symbol, single batch. The interaction coefficient in a negative-binomial GLM is the direct answer, so the plan fits ~ condition + time + condition:time in DESeq2 and tests the interaction Wald coefficient as the primary result. This is the weakest-powered contrast in the design: the interaction is a difference of two differences at n=3 per cell, so its standard error exceeds that of either main effect. The plan therefore reports, side by side and at the same threshold, the simple treatment effect at t0, the simple treatment effect at t1, and the interaction contrast — a gene absent from the interaction list is NOT evidence that its treatment response is the same at both time points, and every downstream step must say so rather than soften the threshold to manufacture hits. Steps run in order: T1S1 sample-structure QC (blind VST, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, sample-distance heatmap, library sizes) to check that the four design cells separate as expected and that no replicate is misplaced before any model is fit; T1S2 the filter, model, interaction test, ashr shrinkage and BH correction in one script; T2S1 preranked fgsea per contrast on the Wald statistic against human Hallmark then Reactome, run separately for the interaction and for each simple effect because a set that moves up at t0 and down at t1 cancels in a pooled list; T1S3 the assembled report with the fit diagnostics, the explicit power statement, and the reproducibility record. Counts are provided as a matrix rather than Salmon quant files, so no tximport length offsets are available — the plan uses the supplied integer counts directly and the report must state that the gene-length offset step could not be applied, which slightly weakens calls driven by isoform switching. Reference gene sets are confirmed present for human (MSigDB Hallmark 2026.1 and Reactome current); enrichment is interpretive and its loss would not defeat the research question.

acceptance_criteria: Report opens with a direct, power-qualified answer to whether the treatment effect differs between t0 and t1
Simple effect at t0, simple effect at t1 and the interaction contrast are shown side by side per gene, with both reference levels named
MA plot, dispersion plot and p-value histograms included before the gene tables
Explicit power statement at 3 replicates per cell, including that absence from the interaction list is not evidence of an equal effect
Gene tables carry log2FoldChange, shrunken log2FoldChange and lfcSE; ranking is on the shrunken value
Leading-edge genes listed per significant gene set, with overlaps between sets marked, and the method-dependence of enrichment stated
Reproducibility record present: sessionInfo, package versions, seed, gene set collection versions, design formula, contrasts, thresholds, n tested, n significant per contrast
The missing tximport length-offset step is recorded as a limitation
constraints: report: interaction_report = simple_effect_reference, simple_effect_other, interaction_contrast (vignette:DESeq2/1.52.0#interactions)
report: power_statement = expected_power_at_replicate_number (doi:10.1261/rna.053959.115)
report: effect_columns = log2FoldChange, shrunken_log2FoldChange, lfcSE; rank_genes_by = shrunken_log2FoldChange
report: fit_diagnostics = ma_plot, dispersion_plot (vignette:DESeq2/1.52.0#ma-plot)
report: reproducibility_record = session_info, seed, package_versions, collection_version (doi:10.1371/journal.pcbi.1003285)
